headline: Nifty had its best day in two months (+1%), but the RBI rate decision at 10 am is the big test today. Most economists expect the first rate rise since 2023.

mood.label: Neutral
mood.why: The bias score is **+6 out of 100**: the long-term trend points down, but options and sentiment data point up, so the four checks cancel out.

key_points.text: Nifty rose **0.98% to 22,776** on Tuesday, helped by banks and by Brent crude dipping below $100 during Indian hours.
The RBI announces its rate decision at **10:00 am**. Most economists expect the repo rate (the rate RBI lends to banks at) to rise from 5.25% to 5.50%.
Foreign investors (FIIs) sold **₹2,961 crore** of shares, but Indian funds (DIIs) bought ₹5,089 crore, more than covering it.
Nifty is still below its 20, 50 and 200-day averages, and its recent peaks and dips are both getting lower. The **long-term trend is still down**.
Option sellers are guarding **22,700 below and 23,000 above**. A clear move outside this band would show the next direction.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.summary: A strong bounce inside a downtrend; the dashboard sees no clear direction yet.

points.text: The data shows Nifty is about 1.6% below its 20-day average (23,147) and **6.3% below its 200-day average** (24,318). Price trend scores −2, the weakest possible.
Option sellers added many bets that Nifty will not fall below 22,500–22,600. The option-chain check scores **+1.5**, a bullish reading.

The put-call ratio (bets on a fall compared with bets on a rise) jumped from 0.71 to **1.06** in five sessions. My read: more people are willing to sell protection under the market, which usually supports prices.
Only **1 of 4** checks agrees with the neutral view, so the dashboard's confidence is low. The checks pull in opposite directions rather than all sitting in the middle.
India VIX (expected swings) is 13.6, higher than **64%** of the past year and flat this week. Option prices are fairly priced, not cheap and not expensive.

sections.title: What big investors are doing
sections.summary: Foreigners are still very bearish in futures, but they are no longer adding to those bets.

points.text: FIIs sold ₹2,961 crore in cash shares. NSDL data shows they sold about **₹35,900 crore** across sectors in September, with banks and finance hit hardest (₹13,147 crore).
Domestic funds bought **₹5,089 crore**, about 1.7 times what FIIs sold. This local buying is the main reason the market held up.

Only **8.5%** of FIIs' index-futures positions are bets on a rise, up a little from 8.0% last week. Below 10% is where, in the past, FIIs have often started buying back their short bets (bets on a fall).
Nifty futures rose ~1% while the number of open contracts fell **1.2%**. This suggests some traders closed bets on a fall, not that fresh buyers rushed in.
FIIs raised their share of bought index puts (insurance against a fall) to **72%**, up 5.4 points. They are still paying for protection.

sections.title: What the world is telling India
sections.summary: US stocks are at records, but high US bond rates, a strong dollar and costly oil still weigh on India.

points.text: The S&P 500 rose about **0.7%** to a record high, led by tech, as oil prices and US bond rates eased. Strong global moods usually help Indian stocks over time.
The US 10-year bond rate is **5.27%**, near its highest in 24 years. When safe US bonds pay this much, foreign money tends to leave markets like India.
Brent crude fell below $100 during Indian hours but ended the US day near **$100.9**, still up 29% in three months. India imports most of its oil, so this is a big cost.
The rupee is weak at **₹96.29 per dollar**, about 1.9% weaker in a month. A weaker rupee cuts the returns foreign investors get in dollars.
Short-term US bills pay 4.30% vs the Fed rate of 3.88%, so the market still prices a **Fed rate rise**. That expectation eased a little this week.

sections.title: Company results
sections.summary: No big companies reported this week; the real results season starts with TCS on Thursday.

points.text: The 20 results filed in the last 7 days are all **small companies**, and none are in the Nifty 50. They tell us little about the index.
Most of these filings lack last year's numbers, so I couldn't compare growth. Indo Rama Synthetics showed profit **down 12%** from a year ago.
**TCS reports on 8 October**, then HCL Tech on 12 October. IT companies earn in dollars, so a weak rupee helps them, but their outlook on US demand matters more.
Reporting says hopes for decent second-quarter earnings helped Tuesday's rally. If big results disappoint, that support goes away.

sections.title: What could change the picture
sections.summary: The RBI today, then US Fed minutes tonight, TCS results and India inflation next week.

points.text: **RBI decision today, 10 am.** A 0.25% rise is largely expected. A bigger rise or a tough tone would hurt banks and borrowers; a pause would likely lift them.
US Fed meeting notes come out at **11:30 pm tonight**. Signs of more US rate rises would push US bond rates and the dollar up, bad for FII flows.
India's inflation data comes on **12 October**. It was 4.82% in August, above RBI's 4% target, which is why a rate rise is on the table.
The weekly options expiry is on **13 October**. Prices can swing near the 22,700 and 23,000 levels as those bets close.
What would prove the bounce wrong: a close **below 22,700** with FIIs adding new short bets, or Brent climbing well above $100 again.

levels.note: A close above 23,000 would push call sellers out and could stretch the bounce; a close below 22,700 would break the new floor and put the downtrend back in charge.

watch.text: Opening: GIFT Nifty near 22,761 points to a flat start.
RBI rate decision. A rise to 5.50% is expected; anything more would hurt banks.
RBI Governor's press conference. Listen for hints about further rises.
FII selling vs DII buying after the close. Watch whether FII futures longs climb above 10%.
US Fed meeting minutes. A tougher tone would lift US bond rates and the dollar.

bottom_line: The data shows a strong one-day bounce inside a downtrend that has not been repaired: Nifty is still below all three key averages and FIIs remain heavily bearish in futures. Option sellers and the put-call ratio now lean bullish, so the dashboard's overall score is close to zero (+6) with low confidence. My read is that domestic buying and cheaper oil gave the market some room, but the RBI decision at 10 am decides whether the bounce can reach 23,000. The main risk is a sharper-than-expected rate rise or a strong dollar pushing FIIs to sell harder, which would put 22,700 under pressure.
